What comes up in Bankstown

3 conditions, and each one is handled differently

Every site is scoped on the day. The table is what the work usually involves here rather than a statement about any particular property.

Commercial strip frontage

Bankstown commercial work is usually attached on at least one side, with a footpath in use and neighbouring businesses trading.

How it is handled
Hoarding and traffic management first, agreed hours, then the structure removed in stages with hand work at the party walls.
What does it
Smaller machines working off the footprint, hand tools at the junctions.

Internal strip out ahead of a fit out

A good share of Bankstown work is removing walls, linings and fit out from a building that stays standing.

How it is handled
Hazardous materials cleared first, structural elements identified, then the removal done by hand so nothing retained is disturbed.
What does it
Hand tools and small plant only, with material carried out and loaded at the kerb.

Freestanding houses

Single and double storey brick, brick veneer, fibro and timber. The era matters more than the material, because anything built before 1990 carries a hazardous materials assumption until it is tested.

How it is handled
Hazardous materials removed and cleared first, services disconnected in writing, then the structure taken down and the material separated as it falls.
What does it
Excavator with a demolition grapple, sized to the side access rather than to the house. Zero tail swing where the work runs hard against a boundary.

What shapes the work on these blocks

  • Three kinds of job in one suburb Freestanding houses, walk up unit blocks and commercial frontages, and the approval, the survey and the plant differ on each.
  • Unit block redevelopment Which is a planned sequence rather than a knockdown: survey, disconnections, soft strip, then the structure.
  • Commercial strips with attached neighbours Partial demolition and hand work at the party walls.
  • Pre 1990 stock throughout Residential and commercial alike.

Bankstown ranges from quiet residential streets to busy commercial frontages, and the logistics change with it. On the commercial side, truck standing and traffic management are usually arranged rather than assumed, and the working hours may be set by the surrounding tenancies.

Bankstown questions

What people ask before we start

Do you demolish walk up unit blocks?
Yes. It is licensed work and it runs as a planned sequence with a full hazardous materials survey, written confirmation of service disconnections, a soft strip and then the structure, with material separated for recycling as it comes down.
Can you work outside business hours on a commercial site?
Where the approval allows it, yes. On a commercial strip the hours are frequently the thing that makes the job workable, and it is worth settling before the programme is fixed.
Does the shale ground change what a site cut costs?
It changes the method, and the method sets the rate. Weathered shale generally comes out with a ripper or a toothed bucket rather than a hammer, and the spoil is heavier, wetter and classified differently from sand. Fresh shale and the sandstone bands between the units are hammer work and are priced by the cubic metre.
Is the asbestos removal a separate engagement?
A separate licence, but not a separate engagement. Licensed asbestos removalists carry out the removal and an independent licensed assessor issues the clearance, while Max holds demolition licence AD214737 and runs the programme across all of it.
